title: Sprite2D does not account for `center` or `offset` when culling if the texture is a MeshTexture.
body: ### Tested versions Tested in v4.7.1 ### System information Godot v4.7.1.stable (a13da4feb) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21043.19003) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.94 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description As per the title, a Sprite2D does not seem to not adjust the bounding box for either the `centered` or `offset` properties when it's using a MeshTexture. Therefore, it culls inappropriately. For example, when a centered Sprite2D with a MeshTexture is viewed as a whole, it seems to display fine. However, if viewed in a way that would not show off its bottom-right bounds, the Sprite2D is needlessly culled. The Sprite2D's culling problems are not apparent if `centered` is disabled and `offset` is equal to Vector2.ZERO. Using a Node2D as an anchor can most likely be used as a workaround, but that would simply be much less convenient. ### Steps to reproduce To recreate this issue, simply just apply a MeshTexture to a Sprite2D with the `center` property set to true (The MRP should already include a scene with this setup.). After that, move around the camera in a way that obscures the Sprite2D's bottom-right corner, and the Sprite2D should be incorrectly culled. To quickly and easily create a functioning MeshTexture, convert a textured Sprite2D with `center` set to false into a MeshInstance2D, and copy that node's `mesh` and `texture` properties into a MeshTexture. After that, set `image_size` to match the source texture's size. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mesh-texture-sprite-2d-culling-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31289896/mesh-texture-sprite-2d-culling-issue.zip) The reproduction project here is as minimal as it gets. Just a single scene with a centered Sprite2D using a MeshTexture.
